d: Big-O notation describes the worst-case time or space required by an algorithm to execute as the input size grows.

p: Big-O notation is the mathematical language we use to evaluate how the runtime or space requirements of an algorithm scale as the input size (N) grows towards infinity. We drop constants and lower-order terms because at massive scales, only the fastest-growing term matters.
1. Identify what 'N' is (usually the length of the input array/string).
2. Count the number of nested loops that depend on N.
4. Drop non-dominant terms (e.g., O(N² + N) becomes O(N²)).

def constant(n):
  return n[0] # O(1)

def linear(n):
  for i in n: print(i) # O(N)

def quadratic(n):
  for i in n:
    for j in n: print(i,j) # O(N^2)
Time: Evaluated per function. Space: Auxiliary space (excluding the input array itself).

O(1)   : 🟩🟩🟩🟩🟩 (Flat line)
O(logN): 🟨🟨🟨🟨🟧 (Slow growth)
O(N)   : 🟨🟧🟧🟥🟥 (Linear growth)
O(N^2) : 🟧🟥🟥⬛⬛ (Parabolic growth)
O(2^N) : 🟥⬛⬛⬛⬛ (Vertical explosion)
